turns.text:
`flow.py` reads `sales.csv` with `csv.DictReader`, parses each row into `(region, amount)` (rows with a blank region or amount are skipped), sums them on a 4-worker farm keyed by region so every row of a region lands on the same worker, and a buffering sink prints one `region  total` line sorted by region.

Run it with `python flow.py` in the directory holding `sales.csv`; `build(source=[...])` accepts a list of row dicts for testing, as verified on a sample (east 100.50, north 12.75, south 10.75).

Note the totals only exist once the stream ends (each worker flushes in `on_end`), and amounts are parsed as floats — a malformed number will raise a `NodeError` naming `parse`.
